intro: Binary cross-entropy at logits has a simple residual gradient. Combine that residual with feature columns and a separate bias parameter.
task: Return mean logistic loss and gradients for a linear binary classifier with no regularization.
requirements: features has shape (n,d), labels has shape (n,) with values zero or one, weights has shape (d,), and bias is a scalar.

Set logits=features@weights+bias and probabilities=sigmoid(logits). Return {"loss": mean(logaddexp(0,logits)-labels*logits), "weights": features.T@(probabilities-labels)/n, "bias": mean(probabilities-labels)}.
Use a stable sigmoid for large positive and negative logits. Include the bias gradient separately and average across observations once.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: The derivative of logistic cross-entropy with respect to a logit is prediction probability minus label.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Use the feature transpose to accumulate weight gradients, and average the same residuals for the bias.

explanation: Differentiating the stable logistic loss with respect to a logit gives sigmoid(logit)-label. Multiplying by each feature and averaging applies the chain rule to the weight vector.
Bias shifts every logit by the same amount, so its gradient is the mean residual. This is a parameter gradient, whereas evaluating a loss alone does not identify an update direction.
